invariants.name: high-confidence-probe-without-text
invariants.statement: A record with source=probe and confidence=high must have non-empty text, because probe means a shipped file was examined and the codec was derived from its actual content
invariants.harm: The codec assignment is baseless — no file content was examined despite claiming high confidence. Editing this config via the codec would operate on a hallucinated format.

invariants.name: shell-script-misclassified-as-config
invariants.statement: Executable shell scripts (.sh, .bash, .csh, .ksh, .zsh, .fish) must not be assigned any config codec (keyvalue, ini, yaml, json, xml)
invariants.predicate: path != '' and any(path.endswith('.' + ext) for ext in ['sh','bash','csh','ksh','zsh','fish']) and codec in ['keyvalue','ini','yaml','json','xml']
invariants.harm: Editing via a config codec would corrupt the shell script — key-value parsing loses control flow, shebangs, and comments. Running the mangled script causes unexpected behavior.

invariants.name: low-confidence-config-claim
invariants.statement: Records with confidence=low should not have a non-none codec, because low confidence means the classifier is uncertain this is even a config file
invariants.harm: The system acts on uncertain classifications, applying a config codec to files that may not be configuration at all, leading to silent corruption.

invariants.name: directory-path-no-extension
invariants.statement: A path that ends with its package name and has no file extension is likely a directory, not a single config file
invariants.predicate: path != '' and '/' in path and not any(path.endswith('.' + e) for e in ['sh','bash','csh','ksh','zsh','fish','desktop','conf','cfg','ini','yaml','yml','json','xml','toml','env']) and any(path.endswith('/' + pkg) or path.endswith('/' + pkg + '/') for pkg in packages) and not any(path.endswith('/' + pkg + '.') for pkg in packages)
invariants.harm: Treating a directory as a single config file causes the codec to attempt parsing an entire directory tree, producing meaningless results and potentially corrupting multiple files.

invariants.name: semantic-codec-extension-mismatch
invariants.statement: The assigned codec must be semantically consistent with the file extension — yaml files get yaml, xml files get xml, json files get json, conf/cfg files get ini or keyvalue (not yaml/xml)
invariants.predicate: path != '' and len(path) > 4 and ('.yaml' in path or '.yml' in path) and codec not in ['yaml','none'] and codec not in ['ini','keyvalue','xml','json']
invariants.harm: A YAML file parsed as INI loses YAML-specific constructs (nested maps, lists, multi-line strings). A YAML file parsed as XML is nonsensical. Either way, the file is corrupted on write.

invariants.name: string_no_numeric_minmax
invariants.statement: A record whose type is string must not carry numeric min or max fields, since length bounds are meaningless for directive-value parsing where the parser accepts any string.
invariants.predicate: spec.get('type') == 'string' and isinstance(spec.get('min'), (int, float)) and isinstance(spec.get('max'), (int, float))
invariants.harm: The config-writer will attempt to enforce integer length constraints on a string value, either rejecting valid strings or silently comparing string lengths against the wrong bounds, producing wrong configurations on the host.

invariants.name: no_sentinel_default
invariants.statement: A string-type record whose default is a sentinel placeholder word (empty, none, unset, disabled, not set, notset, n/a, auto) violates the invariant that the default must be the actual value written to the config file, not a human-readable note about the value.
invariants.predicate: spec.get('default') is not None and isinstance(spec.get('default'), str) and spec.get('default').strip().lower() in ('empty', 'none', 'unset', 'disabled', 'not set', 'notset', 'n/a', 'auto')
invariants.harm: The config-writer will literally write the placeholder word (e.g. 'empty') into the config file instead of the real default, causing the daemon to misinterpret the setting — Postfix home_mailbox set to 'empty' means a literal directory named 'empty', not 'no mailbox set'.

invariants.name: nonempty_description
invariants.statement: Every record's description field must be a non-empty, non-whitespace string, because a blank description means the catalog has no documented semantics for the setting and operators cannot reason about it.
invariants.harm: Automated tooling that surfaces settings for review (diff generators, compliance auditors, migration guides) will emit a setting with no context, leading to unreviewed changes or silent acceptance of wrong values on production hosts.

invariants.name: no-duplicate-enum
invariants.statement: No schema field with an enum list may contain duplicate entries.
invariants.predicate: any(len(v.get('enum', [])) > len(set(v.get('enum', []))) for v in schema.values() if isinstance(v, dict))
invariants.harm: Ambiguous intent: consumers cannot know whether the repeated value signals a bug or a deliberate listing, and gonja's Jinja2 engine may silently treat it as either one or two allowed values.

invariants.name: no-unused-schema-parameters
invariants.statement: More than half of the declared schema parameters must actually be referenced in the template body.
invariants.predicate: len(schema) > 0 and sum(1 for k in schema.keys() if not re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(k) + r'(?=[\s|:.(\]])', body)) > len(schema) / 2
invariants.harm: Users are presented with parameters they cannot use; the schema promises configurability that the template never implements, leading to wasted time, confusion, and potential deployment misconfiguration when defaults (which match the shipped file) diverge from real-world values.

invariants.name: list-schema-uses-yaml-list-rendering
invariants.statement: When a schema field has type 'list' and the template iterates over it, each item must be rendered as a YAML list entry (starting with '- ').
invariants.predicate: any(v.get('type') == 'list' and ('{% for' in body and '- ' not in body) for v in schema.values() if isinstance(v, dict))
invariants.harm: A list-type config field rendered as bare values (one per line, no list markers) produces output that parsers cannot distinguish from a sequence of unrelated scalar directives, causing the consumed application to misread individual items as top-level config keys.
